title: The tangled diff
prompt: The checks pass, but the diff contains an unrelated formatting rewrite. What should you do?

setup.text: The date bug is fixed and all checks pass. The diff touches 14 files: one logic change, plus formatting cleanup my editor applied across the rest.

options.label: Keep it; passing checks prove the extra changes are safe.

outcome.text: The date fix turned out to break a different page. Undo it.
The undo takes the formatting changes in 13 other files with it. Everything was saved as one change.

options.verdict: Tests do not make unrelated edits relevant. Extra change makes review harder and recovery less precise.

options.label: Remove the unrelated rewrite, rerun the relevant check, then save the focused change.

outcome.text: Removed the formatting churn and reran the date check: still passing. The saved change is one file, described as “fix release date rollover”.
That I can read, and if we ever undo it, we undo exactly one thing.

options.verdict: The checkpoint now tells one coherent story and can be understood or reverted without dragging unrelated work along.

options.label: Ask the agent whether it feels confident about the formatting.

outcome.text: Yes, I’m confident. The formatting matches the current style guide.
Confidence wasn’t the question. Fourteen files is still fourteen files to review, and thirteen have nothing to do with the fix.

options.verdict: The issue is scope, not confidence. Judge the diff against the brief you approved.
